install-grok.md:
# Installing demo into Grok Build

> **ACTION REQUIRED: trust this folder before relying on it.** Grok Build
> loads a project's instructions, skills, hooks and `[permission]` rules,
> and starts its MCP servers, only in a trusted folder. Verified on grok
> 1.0.34: on a fresh checkout `grok inspect` reports
> `projectTrusted: false` and loads none of the first four. (It still
> *lists* project MCP servers; per the guide the same trust gate decides
> whether they start.) Inert until trusted:
> - `AGENTS.md` instructions
> - the `[mcp_servers]` in `.grok/config.toml`
> - the `[permission]` rules in `.grok/config.toml`
> - `.grok/skills/`
> - `.grok/hooks/demo.json`
>
> Until then these deny rules are **not enforced** (pass them as `--deny`
> flags, section 4, to enforce them without trust):
> - `Read(./.env)`
> - `Bash(rm:*)`
> - `Bash(git push:*)`
>
> Review the files, then trust the folder (section 2).

## 1. Install Grok Build

```bash
curl -fsSL https://x.ai/cli/install.sh | bash
grok --version   # this adapter was verified against grok 1.0.34
grok login
```

## 2. Trust the folder and check what loaded

From the harness root (after reviewing `.grok/` and `AGENTS.md`):

```bash
grok --trust inspect
```

`--trust` records the folder in `~/.grok/trusted_folders.toml`; `inspect`
then lists what Grok loaded without starting a session. You can also
grant trust inside the TUI with `/hooks-trust`. For CI, `GROK_FOLDER_TRUST=0`
turns the folder-trust gate off for that one process — use it only on a
checkout you trust, never on a fork PR, since it also un-gates any
`.grok/hooks` and MCP commands the checkout carries.

Expected in the `grok inspect` output:

- Project Instructions: `AGENTS.md` (printed as `Agents.md` on a case-insensitive disk), plus `CLAUDE.md` if the harness has one; Grok loads both
- MCP Servers: `codeindex` (stdio)
- MCP Servers: `remote` (http)
- Permissions: source `.grok/config.toml`, 5 loaded
- Agents: `reviewer`
- Skills: `code-search`
- Skills: `run-tests`
- Hooks: 3 from `.grok/hooks`

## 3. MCP servers

Registered in `.grok/config.toml`. Grok names their tools
`<server>__<tool>`; `grok mcp doctor <server>` starts a server and checks
its handshake.

- `codeindex`: stdio, `node ./dist/mcp-server.js`
- `remote`: http, `https://example.com/mcp`

`env` values are written verbatim into `.grok/config.toml`, which is
meant to be committed. Put secrets in the environment and reference
them as `${VAR}` (Grok expands `${VAR}` in `env` at load time);
`grok mcp list --json` prints `env` values in cleartext.

- `codeindex`: `LOG_LEVEL`

## 4. Permissions and headless runs

`.grok/config.toml` carries 2 allow and 3 deny rules in the
`[permission]` table. Grok merges rules from every trusted source and
evaluates `deny` before `ask` before `allow`.

`--deny` flags are enforced whether or not the folder is trusted, so a
headless run should repeat the deny rules (the quoting below is for bash,
zsh or PowerShell; `cmd.exe` needs double quotes, and Grok drops a rule it
cannot parse without reporting it):

```bash
grok -p '<task>' --deny 'Read(./.env)' --deny 'Bash(rm:*)' --deny 'Bash(git push:*)'
```

## 5. Hooks

`.grok/hooks/demo.json` registers 3 hook(s). Command hooks run
`node "$GROK_WORKSPACE_ROOT/.claude/helpers/<name>.cjs"`, the same helper
file the Claude Code adapter references; supply it yourself. Grok sends
the event as JSON on stdin and fails open on a crash or timeout, so a
guard must print an explicit `{"decision": "deny", "reason": "…"}`.
If the harness also ships `.claude/settings.json` hooks, Grok loads
those too; set `GROK_CLAUDE_HOOKS_ENABLED=false` to run only these.

Widened matchers:

- `PreToolUse` → `guard`: matcher `Bash(rm *)` is emitted as `Bash`; the argument predicate `rm *` cannot be expressed in a Grok matcher, so the hook runs for every `Bash` call and the helper must filter.

## Claude Code files in the same harness

Grok's `[compat.claude]` layer (on by default) also loads, once the folder
is trusted: `CLAUDE.md` next to `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`,
`.claude/commands/*.md`, and the `permissions` and `hooks` of
`.claude/settings.json`. It does **not** read `mcpServers` from
`.claude/settings.json`, which is why the MCP servers live in
`.grok/config.toml`.

## Autonomous mode (ADR-246)

`maxTurns` maps to `--max-turns`:

```bash
grok -p 'Keep the test suite green' --max-turns 40 --deny 'Read(./.env)' --deny 'Bash(rm:*)' --deny 'Bash(git push:*)'
```

`goal` maps to Grok's goal mode; in the TUI run:

```
/goal Keep the test suite green --budget 200000
```
